Home.faqSectionTitle: FAQ about theory tickets and the exam
Home.faqMistakesQ: How many mistakes are allowed in the category B exam?
Home.faqMistakesA: The B and B1 theory exam has {total} questions and you need {pass} correct answers to pass, so {mistakes} mistakes are allowed. This rule applies since 21 May 2026; before that, 3 mistakes were allowed. Rules for other categories are in the table above.
Home.faqAccountA: No. Tickets, the exam simulation and the study plan work without an account (the plan is then saved only in this browser). An account is needed for the readiness score, exam history, weak topics and the mistake trainer.
Home.faqPlanQ: How does the study plan work?
Home.faqPlanA: You pick a category and a length: 7, 14, 28 days or your own number. The plan spreads the tickets across the days: each day has a rule card, that topic's tickets with AI explanations, and a mixed day test. A new day opens at 04:00 every day, so there is a night's sleep between new lessons.
Home.faqNew3A: The AI explanation explains each ticket according to the law: which rule applies and why. You can also listen to the question as audio. That way you understand the rule instead of memorising answers.
Home.faqNew2Q: How often are the tickets updated?
Home.faqNew2A: Tickets are updated regularly according to the official exam question bank. The exam rules (number of questions and mistakes allowed) follow the 2026 changes.
Home.faqSchoolQ: Can I prepare for the theory test on my own?
Home.faqSchoolA: For categories A and B, self-study is allowed. Categories C and T/S require a certificate from a driver training institution.
Home.faqAfterQ: What happens after I pass theory?
Home.faqAfterA: Next is the practical exam in two stages: first the yard, then the city. For category B you must take the yard stage within 30 calendar days of passing theory. You'll find the yard elements and the city exam questions right here on the site.
Home.faqNew4Q: How is the readiness score (0–100) calculated?
Home.faqNew4A:
It's a 0–100 score for your licence category; you need an account to see it. It shows how likely you are to pass a real exam in that category.

Only full exams count: all topics and the official number of questions. Exams with selected topics and ticket practice don't change the score, but they do count toward topic coverage.

We take your last 20 full exams (recent ones weigh more) and look at how often you answer correctly. From that we estimate your chance of staying within your category's allowed mistakes, so the same accuracy gives a lower score where fewer mistakes are allowed. If you abandon an exam after a mistake, it still counts when the time runs out. After only a few exams the score is cautious: one lucky exam can't show readiness.

You're ready for the real exam when three things are true at once: the score is 85 or more, your last 3 full exams are passed, and you've covered at least 65% of topics. A topic counts as covered when you've answered about 70% of its questions, in exams or ticket practice. Until then the score shows progress, not a guarantee.

Home.ctaText: Build a plan in a minute, no account needed. With an account, your results feed your readiness score.
